APD.thesis_one_line: Global industrial-gas major with an intact oligopoly business, but repeated multibillion-dollar green-hydrogen write-offs are a real capital-discipline red flag.
kill_criteria: A third impairment/asset write-down exceeding $500M pre-tax within the next four fiscal quarters.
Adjusted EPS guidance is cut (vs. the immediately prior range) at any of the next four quarterly releases.
Core segment (ex-impairment) operating margin falls below 22% for two consecutive quarters.
Estimated net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises above ~4.25x (from ~3.7x now).
FY2027 capex guidance re-accelerates above $4.5B without a named, contracted, return-hurdle-cleared customer.
key_adverse_facts: Three GAAP charge events in five fiscal quarters (~$6.6B pre-tax): FQ2 FY25 $2,927.9M (EPS $(7.77)), FQ4 FY25 ~$795M, and FQ3 FY26 up to $2.9B (EPS $(6.47); LCEC exit, 8-K 30 Jun 2026). [DV04 correction: earlier text said ~$2.33B, which is the FQ2 FY25 operating loss.]
Total debt + finance leases roughly doubled in three years ($7.63B FY22 to $17.66B FY25) to fund the now-partly-abandoned hydrogen megaproject program.
Estimated net debt/adjusted EBITDA ~3.7x, above typical industrial-gas peer norms of 2.5-3.5x (my estimate, not company-disclosed).
data_conflicts: None identified versus the b1 quant snapshot beyond the expected distortion: the model's poor momentum/rank read (432/~500) and any GAAP-P/E-based value read are both artefacts of the two impairment quarters, not independent evidence.
APD.confidence_in_thesis: medium (core industrial-gas execution is well evidenced across four quarters of primary filings; the capital-allocation reservation is well evidenced too, but a full 10-K risk-factor diff and Form 4 review were not completed in this pass)

AZO.thesis_one_line: Dominant US auto-parts retailer compounding sales at 7-8% a year, but negative book equity leaves no cushion and EPS growth has decelerated sharply this year.
kill_criteria: Domestic same-store sales turn negative for two consecutive fiscal quarters (from +1.6% to +4.8% now).
Full-year diluted EPS growth (ex-LIFO/ex-tariff one-offs) is negative for a full fiscal year.
Share-repurchase spend falls below $1.5B over a trailing four quarters without a stated capex-driven reason.
A second consecutive year of gross-margin deleverage (ex the identified one-off items).
key_adverse_facts: Stockholders' equity is deeply negative: $(2.78B) as of 9-May-2026 (improving from $(4.46B) a year earlier), a structural feature of decades of debt-funded buybacks that removes any equity cushion. [Corrected 2026-10-08 (DV05): at 2026-08-29 the deficit was $(2,502.5)M vs $(3,414.3)M at 2025-08-30; $(4.46B) was the Feb-2025 balance. FY2026 repurchases were $2.0B vs $1.58B in FY2025 (+27%), so buyback pace did not slow. FY2026 reported diluted EPS is $152.55 (+5.3%).]

FY2026 diluted EPS growth was roughly +5.5% (sum of quarters $152.79 vs FY2025's $144.88), a sharp deceleration from AutoZone's historical mid-teens per-share growth pace, driven by opex deleverage in three of four quarters.
A meaningful share of this year's reported gross-margin swings (LIFO impact, tariff refunds) are company-labelled non-recurring/timing items, not underlying margin improvement.
data_conflicts: The triage note (Q01_triage.json) asserted 'guided EPS growth of 34%' as the reason for advancing AZO; I could not verify this from the filings -- AutoZone issues no EPS guidance, and verified trailing full-year EPS growth was roughly +5.5%, with only the single strongest quarter (Q4 FY26, +15.1% YoY) approaching double digits. This looks like either a misread of one quarter's growth or an unsourced generic-knowledge claim, and is flagged as an unresolved conflict with the triage rationale.
AZO.confidence_in_thesis: medium (revenue/margin/leverage trend well evidenced across four quarters of primary filings; used-car-age cycle sensitivity and Form 4/10-K risk-factor diff not independently verified in this pass)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for AZO, so v1_verdict is null per the wave-2 instruction. My own reverse-DCF (trailing P/E ~18.8x on FY2026 diluted EPS, rough CAPM cost of equity ~8.7%) implies ~3.4%/yr perpetual earnings growth priced in, below my evidence-based base case of ~8-10%/yr if same-store sales and buyback pace hold -- 'below'/cheap on this lens, though the simple P/E-based method is a weaker fit given so much per-share value creation runs through debt-funded buybacks against negative equity. [Corrected 2026-10-08 (DV05): EPS was treated as cash. On FCF (TTM-to-Q3 OCF $3,072.4M less capex $1,439.1M = $1,633M, 3.5% yield; 3.2% after SBC) implied perpetual growth is ~5.2% at ke 8.7% (4.2% at a 7.7% Blume-beta rate) vs 3.4% stated; still below the 8-10% base, gap 3-5 pts not 5-7.]

BAC.thesis_one_line: Second-largest US bank with accelerating earnings growth and low and stable credit costs, but priced at a 15-year-high book multiple with unusually low credit costs.
kill_criteria: Net charge-off ratio rises above 0.65% for two consecutive quarters (vs. 0.47% now).
CET1 (Standardized) falls below 10.5% (vs. 11.2% now) without a clearly stated, temporary reason.
YoY diluted EPS growth turns negative for any quarter (from the current +18%/+25%/+34% accelerating trend) absent a one-off item.
NII growth decelerates to flat-or-negative YoY for two consecutive quarters (from +9-10% now).
P/B rises further into a new multi-year high (>1.45x) without a corresponding rise in delivered ROE above ~12.5%.
key_adverse_facts: P/B of 1.374x sits at the 94.35th percentile of BAC's own 15-year history -- among the richest valuations the stock has carried in over a decade, per the V1 systematic model. [Corrected 2026-10-08 (DV05): 1.374x divided a diluted market cap by total equity including preferred; on common BVPS $39.34 it is 1.44x book and 1.93x tangible book ($29.37).]
Net charge-off ratio (0.47% in 2Q26) is low in absolute and historical terms; credit costs this benign this late in a rate cycle are not obviously durable.

Much of the recent NII acceleration is explicitly attributed by the company to 'fixed-rate asset repricing' -- a one-time structural tailwind that should mechanically fade once the repricing cycle completes, independent of future rate moves.
CET1 (Standardized) has declined from 11.6% (3Q25) to 11.2% (2Q26) as ~$8B/quarter has been returned to shareholders. [Corrected 2026-10-08 (DV05): 2Q25 CET1 was 11.5%; 11.6% was 3Q25.]
data_conflicts: V1's own valuation.json documents an inherited, unresolved data conflict: D3 TTM revenue ($121.1B) vs. Yahoo TTM revenue ($113.9B) differ 5.9%, and the D3 figure implies an implausible >100% EBIT margin; V1 substituted the Yahoo TTM revenue figure. I did not independently re-verify this vendor discrepancy in this pass.

V1's systematic model (P/B/ROE-mean-reversion method) calls BAC 'excessive' with a negative base-case 3-yr return (-1.9%/yr), while the b1 quant factor snapshot ranks BAC 19th of ~500 names on a composite that treats it as statistically cheap. Both are internally valid on their own terms; the tension is that V1's base-case ROE assumption (7.96%, the 15-year median, anchored to the 2011-2021 near-zero-rate decade) sits well below BAC's current and rising ROE run-rate (11.0% to 12.7% over the last three quarters), which is the reconciliation point addressed in the dossier.
BAC.confidence_in_thesis: medium-high (operating trend across four quarters of primary earnings releases is unambiguous and consistent; litigation/Form 4 review not completed in this pass, and the V1 reconciliation involves a judgement call on which ROE base-rate is more representative going forward)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's justified-P/B model (COE 9.58%, implied ROE 12.03%, base case reverting to the 15-year-median ROE of 7.96%) calls BAC 'excessive' with a base-case return of -1.9%/yr, based mainly on P/B sitting at the 94th percentile of its own 15-year history. I agree BAC is fully priced, not undervalued -- but I disagree with the magnitude of V1's base case, because its median-ROE anchor is dominated by the 2011-2021 near-zero-rate decade, while primary-source evidence in this dossier shows BAC's own ROE accelerating for three straight quarters (11.0% to 12.0% to 12.7%). Using a ~12% ROE base case instead of 7.96% gives a fair P/B of roughly 1.37x -- almost exactly today's multiple -- implying a base-case return closer to flat-to-low-single-digits (dividend yield plus modest book-value growth) rather than V1's -1.9%. Net: same direction (fully priced, not cheap), less negative magnitude; verdict capped at INCLUDE-SMALL rather than a full-weight INCLUDE or a WATCH/REJECT. [Corrected 2026-10-08 (DV05): P/B inherited from V1 is 1.374x on total equity incl. preferred; common P/B is 1.44x and P/TBV 1.93x. Priced-in ROE is 12.5% (not 12.03%) vs 12.0% base vs 12.7% latest; justified P/TBV at 2Q26 ROTCE 17.0% is 2.13x (1.92x at the four-quarter average) vs actual 1.93x. in_line retained, leaning slightly above; kill criterion P/B >1.45x is effectively at threshold. Net charge-offs: 3Q25 0.47%, 4Q25 0.44%, 1Q26 0.48%, 2Q26 0.47% (low and stable, not falling).]
